title: AI Benefits Database
scope: A selected collection of publicly reported benefits involving AI, including individual episodes and comparative study results. Each record preserves its unit of observation, beneficiaries, evidence, and questions for replication. Not a census or estimate of prevalence, effectiveness, or net benefit.

records.title: AI-assisted drone helps rescuers find two overdue hikers
records.date_precision: Reported overdue June 23, 2026. Exact rescue date unreported. Official account published June 25, 2026.
records.location: Dead Horse Gap walking track, near Jindabyne, New South Wales, Australia
records.system: Fire and Rescue NSW drone with AI detection software and thermal camera. Model and vendor not identified.
records.observed_outcome: Both hikers were located and guided to safety.
records.ai_contribution: The agency attributes initial identification in the bush to the drone's AI software. Thermal imaging confirmed the find.
records.human_contribution: The drone operator confirmed the find using thermal imagery and used a spotlight to guide Police and State Emergency Service rescuers. The hikers also signaled with a phone light.
records.evidence_type: Official operational report. No independent causal evaluation.
records.evidence_supports: A first-party operational account describes identification, confirmation, and rescue.
records.limitations: The report does not isolate AI's contribution from thermal imaging, the hikers' signal, or rescuers. It does not establish injuries or deaths avoided, or time saved.
records.tradeoffs: No adverse effects are reported. Costs, surveillance implications, and false detections are not evaluated.
records.replication_hypothesis: Test whether trained operators, effective imaging, ground-team coordination, and clear confirmation procedures enable similar rescues.

records.title: AI fire alert precedes the first 911 call near Grass Valley
records.date_precision: Day and local alert time explicitly reported.
records.location: Near Grass Valley, California, United States
records.system: ALERTCalifornia camera network and DigitalPath/CAL FIRE fire-detection AI.
records.observed_outcome: AI alerted at 5:19 a.m. Firefighters were on scene before the first 911 call at 6:01 a.m. The fire remained under a quarter acre.
records.ai_contribution: Detected a possible ignition in the Wolf Mountain 1 camera feed and alerted firefighters.
records.human_contribution: The program uses trained watchstanders to confirm detections. Firefighters responded and contained this fire.
records.evidence_type: First-party program report. No independent causal evaluation.
records.evidence_supports: The university operating the camera program reports the alert, first-call times, and final containment.
records.limitations: Earlier notification and containment are observed. A larger fire, specific losses, or casualties avoided are not established. The comparison is with the first 911 call, not every possible detection route.
records.tradeoffs: No event-specific adverse effects are reported. False alarms, response costs, and surveillance effects are not evaluated.
records.replication_hypothesis: Test whether camera coverage, human confirmation, reliable dispatch, and available crews produce earlier effective responses elsewhere.
records.beneficiaries: Emergency responders received earlier notification. Nearby residents and property were intended downstream beneficiaries, but specific losses avoided are unmeasured.

evidence_basis.verification_limit: The comparator is the first 911 call. No independent causal evaluation establishes response time without AI or losses avoided.

records.ai_attribution: The source explicitly attributes the camera alert to AI. Human confirmation and firefighting remain essential parts of the response.

records.title: Incidental lung cancer diagnosed before planned anti-TNF treatment
records.date_precision: Study period. Individual episode dates are unreported.
records.location: Turkey/India multicenter study. The individual center is unreported.
records.observed_outcome: A 57-year-old man received a stage IB lung adenocarcinoma diagnosis and underwent right upper lobectomy.
records.ai_contribution: Flagged a lung nodule on a chest X-ray obtained before anti-TNF treatment for ulcerative colitis.
records.human_contribution: Clinicians confirmed the finding, pursued imaging and biopsy, and performed surgery.
records.evidence_type: Individual episode within a peer-reviewed five-patient case series
records.evidence_supports: Documents detection, diagnosis, and treatment for Case 1.
records.limitations: No comparator or long-term follow-up. Survival benefit unestablished. AstraZeneca funded the study. One author worked for Qure.ai.
records.tradeoffs: False flags can trigger unnecessary investigations. Accuracy and net benefit cannot be estimated from these selected cases.
records.replication_hypothesis: Clinician review, accessible confirmatory testing, and reliable treatment referrals.
records.intendedness: Intended diagnostic support. The finding was incidental to the original care plan.
records.source_case_identifier: CREATE case series, Case 1 (one of five patients in the same study)
records.benefit_summary: An incidental AI-flagged nodule led to a lung cancer diagnosis and surgical treatment for one patient.
records.stakeholder_detail: One 57-year-old patient, identified as Case 1 in the published case series.

evidence_basis.evidence_design: Individual patient episode within a five-patient case series
evidence_basis.reported_by: Koksal and colleagues in Cureus. AstraZeneca funded the study, and one author was employed by Qure.ai.
evidence_basis.outcome_documentation: Table 1 records the AI flag, subsequent diagnosis of stage IB adenocarcinoma, and right upper lobectomy.
evidence_basis.verification_limit: No untreated comparator or long-term follow-up establishes survival benefit or the outcome without AI.

records.ai_attribution: The study reports an AI flag followed by clinician agreement and further investigation. The incremental benefit over usual review is unmeasured.
records.editorial_classification_note: Classify the documented diagnosis-and-treatment sequence as the favorable outcome. Do not substitute a claim that AI cured cancer or saved a life.

records.title: Higher immediate physics post-test scores with a designed AI tutor
records.location: Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States
records.observed_outcome: Immediate physics test performance improved with the designed AI tutor: an adjusted effect of 0.63 standard deviations versus classroom active learning.
records.human_contribution: Instructors supplied curriculum, correct solutions, scaffolding, prompts, and videos. Students solved problems.
records.evidence_supports: Two lessons with conditions reversed between groups. Reported post-test observations: 142 AI, 174 classroom. The adjusted effect controls for prior proficiency, lesson, test version, and time on task.
records.limitations: One course with a test ceiling. The instructional package included self-pacing, videos, and at-home study. The comparison does not isolate generic AI or establish teacher replacement. Retention and later transfer were not measured.
records.tradeoffs: Any wider deployment assessment would need to consider costs, access, and the reliability of feedback.
records.replication_hypothesis: Test expert-designed lessons, reliable feedback, and structured practice in other populations with delayed assessments.

records.title: Historians reconstructed known Greek inscription text more accurately with Ithaca
records.location: Ancient Greek epigraphy research. Evaluator location unreported
records.observed_outcome: On masked known text, historians’ top-choice reconstruction accuracy was 71.7% with Ithaca, compared with 25.3% unaided.
records.human_contribution: Interpreted alternatives using historical knowledge and searchable textual parallels.
records.evidence_supports: The evaluation removed 1–10 known characters, allowing reconstructions to be checked against the original. Results are reported in Nature, Table 1.
records.limitations: Two trained evaluators do not represent all historians. Accuracy on masked known text does not establish accuracy on genuinely unknown text. The paper’s authors include Ithaca’s developers, and the corpus reflects prior scholarship.
records.tradeoffs: Incorrect reconstructions and uneven corpus coverage are considerations for future use. This record does not estimate their downstream effects.
records.replication_hypothesis: Test representative digitized corpora, expert interpretation, transparent alternatives, and independent contextual checks.
records.beneficiaries: Two graduate historians specializing in Greek history and epigraphy
